description: Optional domain profile for agent operations. This profile is never applied by default and is not part of the Standard Norm: it binds a terminal only when that terminal declares it in norm_profiles at SESSION_START (RFC-0001 Section 9.3). When no declaration is made, only the Standard Norm (rackp.standard.v1) applies. Background: RFC-0002 Section 3, Known Risks and Limitations, 'Unrecorded delegation boundary'.

norms.name: Configuration Identity Anchoring
norms.description: A terminal operating an AI agent under this profile must anchor the hash of the effective instruction set and configuration governing the agent at the start of each session, and must anchor each configuration state it subsequently relies upon before relying on it, so that the configuration in force at the time of any anchored action is determinable post-hoc. This norm does not require the implementation to expose a configuration-change event: the anchoring moments are the terminal's to choose, and an implementation that cannot detect changes satisfies the norm by re-anchoring the state it is about to rely on, an unchanged state yielding an unchanged hash. Anchoring a configuration change is an ordinary anchored action and requires no separate recording channel. The most recently anchored configuration state at or before an anchored action is read as having governed that action until a superseding state is anchored; a terminal that changes the configuration without anchoring the new state therefore asserts, through the record it leaves, that the earlier state governed. The obligation reaches the configuration the terminal controls or can observe — where the effective instruction set incorporates elements it neither controls nor observes, such as provider-side instructions, a model version changed behind a stable endpoint, or remotely delivered configuration, the terminal discloses that boundary rather than anchoring what it cannot see. Anchoring is hash-only: the payload is not disclosed to the Keeper, and this profile does not define the payload format — any serialization with a canonical form is acceptable, since the protocol commits only to data_hash. An Actor's anchors carry no action_type (RFC-0001 Section 6.1), so a record is established as a configuration record by disclosing its payload against the anchored data_hash, not by inspection of the ledger alone. The Norm Profile in force is declared separately at session start under STD-009; this norm concerns the agent's own configuration, not the norm declaration. An anchored action whose governing configuration is not covered by any anchored record is recorded as a disclosed gap in the delegation boundary record, not as a technical violation (RACKP-AGENTOPS-004).

norms.name: Tool Authority Anchoring
norms.description: A terminal operating an AI agent under this profile must anchor the authority state on which each anchored action relies — the delegation, token, or other artifact conferring the tool, permission scope, or capability used — before the action that relies on it. Delegation artifacts carry their own validity claims, so anchoring the artifact records the window its issuer declared; no separate grant event is required, and this norm does not depend on the implementation exposing one. Revocation is anchored as observed. The terminal is a verifier, not the issuer: it learns of a revocation through a periodic list, an online query, or a pushed event, and cannot witness the moment the revocation took effect. It must therefore anchor the revocation together with the time and channel of its own observation, and must not present an issuer's asserted effective time as its own observation. What these records establish is the authority state presented to or observed by the terminal and the point at which it relied on that state — not the instant at which authority changed. The interval between an issuer's declared effective time and the terminal's observation is part of the record and is preserved rather than collapsed into a single time, because whether the terminal could have known of a revocation before relying on the capability is a distinct question from whether the capability was still in force. Anchoring is hash-only; this profile does not define the payload format, and a record is established as an authority record by disclosing its payload against the anchored data_hash. An authority record that is not anchored, or that is not disclosed, is recorded as a disclosed gap in the delegation boundary record, not as a technical violation (RACKP-AGENTOPS-004).

norms.name: Human Approval Anchoring
norms.description: A terminal operating an AI agent under this profile must anchor each human approval event for an action that requires human sign-off, bound to the action it authorizes. The binding must be carried inside the signed approval payload: an approval whose reference to the authorized action is not covered by its own signature can be presented for a different action, and does not satisfy this norm. The binding derivation must further be fully specified and available to the verifier — including the exact representation, or the encoding or canonicalization rule used to derive the reference — so that a party other than the signer can recompute it from the disclosed action. Where the binding is intended to be stable across equivalent structured serializations, the derivation must use a specified canonical encoding or another normatively defined representation that yields the same bytes across implementations; absent that, two implementations may derive different references for the same action merely because they serialized its members in a different order. This profile prescribes neither the representation nor the canonical form — the artifact's own schema determines them — but the method must be determinable by the verifier from what is disclosed. Anchoring is hash-only; this profile does not define the payload format. A required approval that is not anchored, or is anchored with a binding that is absent, unsigned, or not recomputable as above, is recorded as a disclosed gap in the delegation boundary record, not as a technical violation (RACKP-AGENTOPS-004).

norms.name: Delegation Boundary Disclosure
norms.description: When assessing an incident under this profile, the Referee must record in evidence_sufficiency which of the artifact classes required by RACKP-AGENTOPS-001 through RACKP-AGENTOPS-003 were available for the interval of the incident action, listing each absent class in gaps, and must state in detailed_report which classes were present and what the available record did and did not establish. Availability is determined from the payloads disclosed against anchored data_hash values, since an Actor's anchors do not name their class; an anchor present in the ledger but withheld from submission surfaces as a disclosed gap (RFC-0001 Section 6.27). Absence of a required artifact class must not be factored into the fault values and must not be listed in technical_violation — the same boundary STD-010 and STD-030 draw for fee compliance and participation status. Its consequences flow from the evidence, not from a penalty: an absent record establishes nothing, and that shortfall is reflected through evidence_sufficiency and assessment_status, and may be reflected in fault.confidence where the Referee documents the basis for departing from the reference value (RFC-0001 Section 7). This profile takes no position on apportionment within the Actor side (model vendor, operator, configurator), which remains with contract and judicial layers; its function is to preserve the boundary evidence that makes such apportionment possible.
